title: Pioneer Venus Day Probe on Venus

height.product: Venus Magellan Global Topography 4641m v2 (GTDR altimetry)

color.product: Venus Magellan SAR left-look global mosaic 75m (partial coverage; gap filled with synthetic filler, see note)

note: Shows the Day Probe touchdown 1978-12-09 at 31.3 S, 317 E (NSSDCA 1978-078G); it kept transmitting for 67 min after landing. The other two small probes landed far away (North Probe 59.3 N, 4.8 E; Night Probe 28.7 S, 56.7 E) and have no tile. Colour is Magellan radar brightness (roughness), not visible light; the real ground is lit dim orange under thick clouds. Height is ~4.6 km/px altimetry upsampled to a ~98 m grid, so it only shows broad slopes. Projection: local tangent plane, north up. Coordinates are the NSSDCA-listed touchdown points; the probes were not tracked to the ground precisely, so the site is approximate (tens of km). Magellan has NO radar coverage over 72% of this tile (the western part); that area is neutral filler (topography shading + random speckle), not imagery.
gravity_note: Venus's gravity is 91% of Earth's, but the air is 90 times thicker and hot enough (465 C) to melt lead.
